ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the pentagon ABCDE is a regular pentagon, and F, G are points on the sides CD, DE, respectively, with BF$\parallel$AG. If $\angle$CFB$=57^\circ$, what is the value of $\angle$AGD?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since pentagon ABCDE is a regular pentagon, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$D=$180^\circ \times 3 \div 5=108^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle$CFB=$57^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BFD=$180^\circ - \angle$CFB=$180^\circ - 57^\circ =123^\circ$, \\
Since BF$\parallel$AG, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BAG+$\angle$FBA=$180^\circ$, \\
In pentagon ABFDG, \\
$\therefore$ $540^\circ=\angle$BAG+$\angle$FBA+$\angle$BFD+$\angle$D+$\angle$AGD=$180^\circ+123^\circ+108^\circ+\angle$AGD, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AGD=\boxed{129^\circ}.
